comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier automated review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13064#issuecomment-5805227549), checked at `681187ea` ("fix: address review on panel plugin api refresh").

**Verified:** the three code findings from the earlier review are resolved at this head, and no regression was found in the changed or shared code. The PR description is still outdated, and the new `active` guard has no test coverage.

| Earlier finding | Status at `681187ea` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Menu panel gets a facade without `appLibrary` at load | Resolved | `onLoaded` now builds the facade from `pluginRegistry.installedPlugins[id]`, whose `kinds` is a real JS array, instead of the `Instantiator` copy |
| Revokes inside `createScopedPluginShell()` are not re-delivered | Resolved | The panel, `pluginShellForId()` (`Bar.qml`), `ensureService()` and `_syncServices()` all pass the registry manifest, so they compute the same profile and share one cached facade instead of revoking each other's |
| Refresh also runs for disabled plugins | Resolved | `prunePluginApis()` now refreshes only `if (active)`, so a disabled plugin's panel gets no new facades, whichever `pluginsChanged` handler runs first |
| Description accuracy | Still present | See below |

**Verified:** the earlier diagnosis of the load-time cause holds. In the Qt Declarative 6.11.2 source, `Instantiator` converts the JS model with `QJSValue::toVariant()`, and the nested `kinds` list reads back in the delegate as a `QV4::Sequence`, for which `Array.isArray()` is false. The shared `deliverPanelPluginApis()` helper assigns the same properties as the old `onLoaded`. The refresh now also sets `omarchyPath` and `service`, which matches `onLoaded`. First-party panels still receive the host shell.

**Description accuracy:** the PR body still says a revoke nulls `shell`, `manifest`, `barWidgetRegistry` and `pluginRegistry`. It also says disabled plugins are skipped by the `installedPlugins` lookup. `revokePluginShellApi()` destroys the scoped `shell` facade and its proxies (including `appLibrary`), not all four properties. Disabled plugins are now skipped by the new `active` guard. The body does not mention the `onLoaded` change, which is now the main fix for the empty grid. **Suggested change:** update the description to say that the revoke destroys the scoped `shell` facade and its proxies, that the `active` guard skips disabled plugins, and that the `onLoaded` registry-manifest change fixes the load-time `appLibrary` loss.

**Optional test improvement:** the updated `test/shell.d/plugin-auth-boundary-test.sh` catches a revert of the `onLoaded` wiring, but it still passes when `if (active)` or the whole refresh call is removed from `prunePluginApis()`. One assertion in the file's existing style covers both. In an isolated run it matched this head and failed on the earlier head, on base and on both mutations:

```bash
qml_matches "$shell_qml" 'shell\.revokePluginShellApi\( *shellKey *\)[^}]*if *\( *active *\) *shell\.refreshPanelPluginApis\(' ||
  fail "only active plugins receive refreshed panel apis after a revoke"
```

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of `shell/shell.qml`, `PluginRegistry.qml`, `PluginShellApi.qml` and `Bar.qml` at this head, the earlier reviewed head and base, plus the Qt Declarative 6.11.2 conversion path. The PR's own static test was run in an isolated sandbox against each revision and against diagnostic mutations. Its unrelated Node-based `AuthServiceStore.js` block was removed because Node was not available there, and the compositor part skips as shipped. No QML runtime harness was run at this head, so the runtime conclusions rest on source reading. The Quickshell runtime, a live desktop session and other Qt versions were not exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this follow-up, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
